title: Erdős Problem #116 — Area enclosed by a polynomial lemniscate
statement:
For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $z_1,\ldots,z_n\in\overline{\mathbb D}:=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|\le 1\}$, with repetitions allowed, and let $p(z)=\prod_{i=1}^n(z-z_i)$ be the resulting monic polynomial. Write $m_2$ for planar Lebesgue measure and set
$$
A(p):=m_2\bigl(\{z\in\mathbb C:|p(z)|<1\}\bigr).
$$
The question is whether there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that, for every $n\ge 2$ and every such choice of zeros,
$$
A(p)>c n^{-C},
$$
and, more strongly, whether there are absolute constants $c',C'>0$ such that
$$
A(p)>c'(\log n)^{-C'}.
$$ [Erdős Problems #116](https://www.erdosproblems.com/116) [Erdős (1982)](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf)

## Background

The area-minimization problem arose in Erdős’s work on geometric properties of polynomials. The 1940 version concerned the part of the unit-level lemniscate inside the unit disk, with zeros on the unit circle; Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian later studied the full lemniscate with the same restriction on the zeros. They showed that the minimum area tends to zero with the degree, and Erdős’s 1982 account asks for its rate of decay. [On the area of polynomial lemniscates](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.18270v1) [Erdős (1982)](https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1982-33.pdf)

Restricting the zeros to a bounded region is essential: without such a constraint the area can be made arbitrarily small by separating the zeros. The full lemniscate also has a contrasting universal upper bound: Pólya proved that its area is at most $\pi$, with equality only when all zeros coincide. [On the area of polynomial lemniscates](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.18270v1) [Erdős Problems #116](https://www.erdosproblems.com/116)

## Known results

Pommerenke’s 1961 result gives a uniform lower bound of order $n^{-4}$. For upper bounds on the minimum, Wagner constructed examples with area $\ll_\epsilon (\log\log n)^{-1/2+\epsilon}$ for every $\epsilon>0$; Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran subsequently improved this to $\ll (\log\log n)^{-1}$. They also proved the logarithmic lower bound, so the proposed polynomial and polylogarithmic lower bounds hold. [Erdős Problems #116](https://www.erdosproblems.com/116) [On the area of polynomial lemniscates](https://arxiv.org/html/2503.18270v1)

A 2026 preprint establishes the sharp order. If $\kappa_n(K,1)$ denotes the infimum of the unit-level lemniscate area over monic degree-$n$ polynomials with zeros in $K$, then, for every $n\ge 3$, it proves
$$
\frac{c}{\log n}\le \kappa_n(\overline{\mathbb D},1)\le \kappa_n(\mathbb T,1)\le \frac{C}{\log n},
$$
for absolute constants $c,C>0$. The lower bound is attributed there to Krishnapur, Lundberg, and Ramachandran; the preprint’s new upper bound holds even when every zero is required to lie on the unit circle. Thus the infimum for zeros in the closed disk has order $1/\log n$, and the same order is attained up to constants under the unit-circle restriction. [Sharp order in Erdős’s minimum-area problem for polynomial lemniscates (2026 preprint)](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.17097)
